Christianity became the official religion of the Roman Empire in 380 AD under Emperor Theodosius I [d1, d3, d6, d8, d9]. Specifically, the Edict of Thessalonica was issued on February 27, 380, declaring Christianity the state religion [d3]. This marked the culmination of a process that began earlier in the century under Constantine [d2, d4, d7]. [[END-OF-ANSWER]]
